text:
Passive movements are joint movements produced entirely by an external force, such as a therapist, a machine, or the patient's other limb, while the patient's muscles stay relaxed. They are used to maintain range of motion, reduce stiffness, and assess joint mobility. The team note is right that the patient contributes no effort, but it is wrong to say these movements stop short of the end of range, since clinicians often take the joint to end range and may apply gentle overpressure.
